user: I'm CUS-0004. Transaction TX-0401, 240.00 EUR: the goods never arrived. Which reason code applies?
answer:
The reason code that matches your situation is **goods_not_received**. It applies when a purchase was paid for but the goods were never delivered.

According to Verta's dispute rules, this code has a **90-day window counted from the transaction date**. A dispute opened after that window closes is not eligible. I have not yet checked the date of TX-0401, so I can't confirm it is still within the window.

If you'd like to proceed, I can check TX-0401's eligibility under this code. If it is eligible, I can open the dispute for the full 240.00 EUR, but I'll confirm with you before filing.

fragments.text:
Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Reason code guide
## Choosing a code
The reason code must match what actually happened. A dispute filed under the
wrong code is declined and must be refiled, which may push it past its window.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Glossary
## Reason code
The classification of why a transaction is disputed. The reason code determines
the chargeback window and the evidence required.
